# Review packet P3-general_information-01

Priority P3, domain general_information, 40 items. Status of every item: not approved.

**How to review independently:** answer every item below before opening the answer sheet. Then compare, and mark each item ACCEPT / FIX (say what) / REJECT in `decisions.csv` (one row per id). Do not edit the item files; the bank worker applies fixes as draft replacements.

**Check for this domain:** Open the source_url and find the quoted text. Does it support the key exactly, and is the law still current (no amendment)?

## Answer sheet (open only after answering)

### 1. `CIVIO-D1022-GI-0001`: key (A) Civil servants may not engage in electioneering or partisan political campaigns

- Why correct: "Civil servants may not engage in electioneering or partisan political campaigns" is correct. Art. IX-B, Sec. 2(4) bans civil servants from campaigning directly or indirectly, and doing it on a lunch break is still campaigning. Source checked word for word against the 1987 Constitution text on lawphil.net.
- (B) Nothing bars a civil servant from voting; the ban is on campaigning.
- (C) The same section protects self-organization; joining a union is allowed.
- (D) That is the double-office rule of Sec. 7, not the campaign ban.
- Source: 1987 Const., Art. IX-B, Sec. 2(4) <https://lawphil.net/consti/cons1987.html>; quote: "No officer or employee in the civil service shall engage, directly or indirectly, in any electioneering or partisan political campaign"
- File: `docs/research/batches/drafts/gi-applied-2026-10-22.json`

### 2. `CIVIO-D1022-GI-0002`: key (A) Their right to self-organization shall not be denied

- Why correct: "Their right to self-organization shall not be denied" is correct. Government employees keep the right to form unions and associations under Art. IX-B, Sec. 2(5). Source checked word for word against the 1987 Constitution text on lawphil.net.
- (B) The guarantee covers government employees in general.
- (C) Art. IX-B, Sec. 2(5) and Art. III, Sec. 8 both cover public employees.
- (D) The Constitution sets no such condition; the right may not be denied.
- Source: 1987 Const., Art. IX-B, Sec. 2(5) <https://lawphil.net/consti/cons1987.html>; quote: "The right to self-organization shall not be denied to government employees"
- File: `docs/research/batches/drafts/gi-applied-2026-10-22.json`

### 3. `CIVIO-D1022-GI-0003`: key (D) No civil servant may be removed or suspended except for cause provided by law

- Why correct: "No civil servant may be removed or suspended except for cause provided by law" is correct. Security of tenure means a lawful cause is needed before a civil servant is suspended or removed. Source checked word for word against the 1987 Constitution text on lawphil.net.
- (A) No discretionary suspension period exists; cause is required.
- (B) Notice alone does not supply the legal cause the Constitution requires.
- (C) The rule protects officers and employees of the civil service.
- Source: 1987 Const., Art. IX-B, Sec. 2(3) <https://lawphil.net/consti/cons1987.html>; quote: "No officer or employee of the civil service shall be removed or suspended except for cause provided by law"
- File: `docs/research/batches/drafts/gi-applied-2026-10-22.json`

### 4. `CIVIO-D1022-GI-0004`: key (A) Merit and fitness, determined as far as practicable by competitive examination

- Why correct: "Merit and fitness, determined as far as practicable by competitive examination" is correct. Art. IX-B, Sec. 2(2) requires merit and fitness, usually tested by a competitive exam except for policy-determining, primarily confidential or highly technical posts. Source checked word for word against the 1987 Constitution text on lawphil.net.
- (B) Endorsements are not the constitutional basis of appointment.
- (C) Residence is not a constitutional basis for civil service appointment.
- (D) Age is not the measure; merit and fitness is.
- Source: 1987 Const., Art. IX-B, Sec. 2(2) <https://lawphil.net/consti/cons1987.html>; quote: "Appointments in the civil service shall be made only according to merit and fitness"
- File: `docs/research/batches/drafts/gi-applied-2026-10-22.json`

### 5. `CIVIO-D1022-GI-0005`: key (A) He cannot be appointed to any government office within one year after the election

- Why correct: "He cannot be appointed to any government office within one year after the election" is correct. Art. IX-B, Sec. 6 bars a losing candidate from any government appointment, including GOCCs, for one year after the election. Source checked word for word against the 1987 Constitution text on lawphil.net.
- (B) The period is one year, not three.
- (C) The bar covers GOCCs and their subsidiaries as well.
- (D) Canvassing does not end the bar; it runs for one year.
- Source: 1987 Const., Art. IX-B, Sec. 6 <https://lawphil.net/consti/cons1987.html>; quote: "No candidate who has lost in any election, shall within one year after such election, be appointed to any office in the Government"
- File: `docs/research/batches/drafts/gi-applied-2026-10-22.json`

### 6. `CIVIO-D1022-GI-0006`: key (B) An elective official is not eligible for appointment to any public office during his tenure

- Why correct: "An elective official is not eligible for appointment to any public office during his tenure" is correct. Art. IX-B, Sec. 7 makes elective officials ineligible for appointment or designation to another public office while they serve. Source checked word for word against the 1987 Constitution text on lawphil.net.
- (A) Council approval cannot lift a constitutional disqualification.
- (C) The bar is on the appointment itself, paid or not.
- (D) The rule covers any public office or position.
- Source: 1987 Const., Art. IX-B, Sec. 7 <https://lawphil.net/consti/cons1987.html>; quote: "No elective official shall be eligible for appointment or designation in any capacity to any public office or position during his tenure"
- File: `docs/research/batches/drafts/gi-applied-2026-10-22.json`

### 7. `CIVIO-D1022-GI-0007`: key (B) He may not receive additional, double, or indirect compensation unless a law specifically authorizes it

- Why correct: "He may not receive additional, double, or indirect compensation unless a law specifically authorizes it" is correct. Art. IX-B, Sec. 8 bars double or indirect compensation unless a specific law authorizes it. Source checked word for word against the 1987 Constitution text on lawphil.net.
- (A) Declaring income does not make unauthorized pay lawful.
- (C) The source of the money does not change the rule.
- (D) Only a specific law can authorize extra compensation.
- Source: 1987 Const., Art. IX-B, Sec. 8 <https://lawphil.net/consti/cons1987.html>; quote: "No elective or appointive public officer or employee shall receive additional, double, or indirect compensation, unless specifically authorized by law"
- File: `docs/research/batches/drafts/gi-applied-2026-10-22.json`

### 8. `CIVIO-D1022-GI-0008`: key (D) The consent of Congress

- Why correct: "The consent of Congress" is correct. Art. IX-B, Sec. 8 requires the consent of Congress before any public officer accepts a present, emolument, office or title from a foreign government. Source checked word for word against the 1987 Constitution text on lawphil.net.
- (A) Acceptance without the consent of Congress is barred.
- (B) The Constitution names Congress, not a department.
- (C) The CSC is not the body that gives this consent.
- Source: 1987 Const., Art. IX-B, Sec. 8 <https://lawphil.net/consti/cons1987.html>; quote: "nor accept without the consent of the Congress, any present, emolument, office, or title of any kind from any foreign government"
- File: `docs/research/batches/drafts/gi-applied-2026-10-22.json`

### 9. `CIVIO-D1022-GI-0009`: key (A) Take an oath or affirmation to uphold and defend the Constitution

- Why correct: "Take an oath or affirmation to uphold and defend the Constitution" is correct. Art. IX-B, Sec. 4 requires every public officer and employee to take an oath or affirmation to uphold and defend the Constitution. Source checked word for word against the 1987 Constitution text on lawphil.net.
- (B) Union membership is a right, not a requirement.
- (C) The Ombudsman issues no such pre-service requirement in the Constitution.
- (D) This may be an agency requirement but it is not the constitutional duty.
- Source: 1987 Const., Art. IX-B, Sec. 4 <https://lawphil.net/consti/cons1987.html>; quote: "All public officers and employees shall take an oath or affirmation to uphold and defend this Constitution"
- File: `docs/research/batches/drafts/gi-applied-2026-10-22.json`

### 10. `CIVIO-D1022-GI-0010`: key (C) Public office is a public trust

- Why correct: "Public office is a public trust" is correct. Art. XI, Sec. 1 says public office is a public trust and that officials must be accountable to the people and lead modest lives. Source checked word for word against the 1987 Constitution text on lawphil.net.
- (A) State immunity is unrelated to how an officer uses funds.
- (B) That principle concerns the armed forces, not public funds.
- (D) Religion is not involved in the scenario.
- Source: 1987 Const., Art. XI, Sec. 1 <https://lawphil.net/consti/cons1987.html>; quote: "Public office is a public trust"
- File: `docs/research/batches/drafts/gi-applied-2026-10-22.json`

### 11. `CIVIO-D1022-GI-0011`: key (D) To lead modest lives

- Why correct: "To lead modest lives" is correct. Art. XI, Sec. 1 tells public officers to be accountable, act with patriotism and justice, and lead modest lives. Source checked word for word against the 1987 Constitution text on lawphil.net.
- (A) This is an election requirement, not an Art. XI duty.
- (B) Patriotism is listed, but the scenario is about extravagance.
- (C) Term length is in Art. X, not a conduct duty.
- Source: 1987 Const., Art. XI, Sec. 1 <https://lawphil.net/consti/cons1987.html>; quote: "act with patriotism and justice, and lead modest lives"
- File: `docs/research/batches/drafts/gi-applied-2026-10-22.json`

### 12. `CIVIO-D1022-GI-0012`: key (C) No; officers not listed in Sec. 2 are removed as provided by law, not by impeachment

- Why correct: "No; officers not listed in Sec. 2 are removed as provided by law, not by impeachment" is correct. Impeachment is reserved for the President, Vice-President, Supreme Court Members, Constitutional Commission Members and the Ombudsman. Source checked word for word against the 1987 Constitution text on lawphil.net.
- (A) Graft is a ground; the issue is the removal route.
- (B) Only the officials named in Sec. 2 are impeachable.
- (D) The Senate tries impeachments but cannot impeach a bureau director.
- Source: 1987 Const., Art. XI, Sec. 2 <https://lawphil.net/consti/cons1987.html>; quote: "All other public officers and employees may be removed from office as provided by law, but not by impeachment"
- File: `docs/research/batches/drafts/gi-applied-2026-10-22.json`

### 13. `CIVIO-D1022-GI-0013`: key (D) Yes; the Ombudsman acts promptly on complaints filed in any form or manner

- Why correct: "Yes; the Ombudsman acts promptly on complaints filed in any form or manner" is correct. The Ombudsman and Deputies, as protectors of the people, act promptly on complaints filed in any form or manner. Source checked word for word against the 1987 Constitution text on lawphil.net.
- (A) No counsel requirement exists in Sec. 12.
- (B) The Constitution says any form or manner.
- (C) Complaints against any government official are covered.
- Source: 1987 Const., Art. XI, Sec. 12 <https://lawphil.net/consti/cons1987.html>; quote: "shall act promptly on complaints filed in any form or manner against public officials or employees of the Government"
- File: `docs/research/batches/drafts/gi-applied-2026-10-22.json`

### 14. `CIVIO-D1022-GI-0014`: key (C) Yes; it may investigate on its own any act that appears illegal, unjust, improper, or inefficient

- Why correct: "Yes; it may investigate on its own any act that appears illegal, unjust, improper, or inefficient" is correct.
